Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - benchmarks & next steps

Alex — great to speak earlier. Per our convo I put together a draft MAP milestone for the technical evaluation so we have clear success criteria and owners. High-level below, full draft attached (acme-map-draft-v2.pdf) and a latency/cost bench template (latency-bench-template.xlsx).

Technical evaluation milestone (owner: Redwood + Acme):
- Goal: Validate model/serving config meets production SLOs for customer-facing summarization
- Success criteria (pass = all must be met):
  * 99th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for 1-3 sentence summaries (p50 <= 120ms)
  * Tokenized cost <= $0.0025 per generated token at target concurrency (after recommended batching/caching)
  * Output quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 vs Acme reference set AND manual review pass-rate >= 92% on 100 sampled summaries
  * Memory/KV/cache footprint within Acme infra constraints (detailed in attached traffic profile)
- Model shortlist (initial):
  * flan-t5-xl (quantized) — Redwood-managed
  * redwood-mini-2.1 (optimized) — Redwood-managed
  * openchat-alpha (baseline) — customer-provided/fallback
- Eval plan & timeline:
  1) Day 0–3: Data ingestion & synthetic workload setup (owner: Acme + Redwood)
  2) Day 4–7: Baseline runs and kernel tuning (owner: Redwood)
  3) Day 8–10: A/B quality evals + manual review (owner: Acme)
  4) Day 11–14: Final tuning and report (owner: Redwood)
- Dependencies:
  * Acme provides 10k sample requests + config and acceptance test set by EOD Wed
  * Access to Acme test VPC or sample dataset upload to shared Drive (link in email)
  * Procurement sign-off on POC capacity booking (see procurement@acme.com)
- Target close / sign-off: Sept 10, 2027 (mutual acceptance of performance report)

Next steps (for this week):
1) Acme: confirm sample data delivery timeline (Alex)
2) Redwood: schedule bench runs and share access instructions (Camila)
3) Procurement alignment: Alex to loop procurement on capacity booking

If that looks right I'll update the MAP doc with owners + dates and send an editable link. Happy to hop on a 30m sync if you prefer.

Thanks,

Alex — looping in Rishi (inference infra) to call out a couple of config items and confirm infra assumptions. Rishi — two quick asks before we kick off:

1) Can you confirm if Acme can permit test VPC access for 10k synthetic requests OR if you prefer uploading data to the shared Drive? Either is fine but we need the mechanism to ensure KV/cache consistency.
2) For the latency target above (99p <= 450ms), is Acme planning to use single-region latency SLOs or customer-edge routing? That affects model shard placement and batching windows.

Rishi — any recommended initial batch size and quantization profile we should try first for flan-t5-xl to hit the cost target?

On schedule: once data is confirmed we'll spin up the bench cluster and run baseline within 48–72 hours.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan - benchmarks & next steps

Thanks — quick responses inline.

> Can you confirm if Acme can permit test VPC access or upload to Drive?
Either works. Prefer VPC for fidelity; Drive upload is acceptable for initial runs if procurement/VPC will take longer.

> Single-region SLO vs edge routing?
If Acme expects <500ms 99p from their primary US-west region, we'll optimize single-region placement first. If multi-region edge routing is required we will need additional capacity and ~3 more business days for cross-region tuning.

Recommended starting config (to meet cost/latency target):
- Model: flan-t5-xl quantized to int8 + Redwood kernel optimizations
- Batch window: adaptive, target 40–60ms (keeps p50 low while enabling batching for cost)
- KV cache policy: prefix caching for repetitive prompts (we'll instrument cache hit-rate)
- Expected token cost (projected): ~$0.0022/token after batching & cache at observed concurrency

I'll prepare a quick runbook and push the bench cluster configs to the Drive link today. If Alex can confirm data delivery timeline we can lock the Day 0 start.

— Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
